DNA is made up of a sequence of four types of building blocks, called adenine, cytosine, guanine and thymine, that come in 4 possible variations (A,T,G,C).  Random copying errors can cause a mutation down to one of these four types, so that somewhere in the genetic sequence, there is a mistake or change in one of these building blocks.  Over time, random mutations can accumulate in a population or species, and can sometimes be harmful or cause disease, or sometimes be beneficial or evolutionarily adaptive.
